chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from his father, from Harun ibn al-Jahm, from al-Mufaddal ibn Salih, from Sa'd ibn Taref, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

Injustice (al-zulm) is of three types: an injustice which Allah forgives, an injustice which Allah does not forgive, and an injustice which Allah does not leave (unpunished). As for the injustice which He does not forgive, it is Shirk (associating partners with Him). And as for the injustice which He does forgive, it is the injustice of a person to himself, in what is between him and Allah. And as for the injustice which He does not leave (unpunished), it is al-mudayanah (claims/due rights) between the servants.

key_terms.الْمُدَايَنَةُ: Claims, dues, or rights between people

ai.seo_question: What are the three types of injustice in Shia hadith and how does God respond to each?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Kafi, Imam al-Baqir (AS) delineates three categories of zulm based on divine retribution: Shirk, which is unforgiven; personal sins between the individual and God, which are forgiven; and rights of others (al-mudayanah), which are not left unpunished. This classification underscores the Shia theological emphasis on the necessity of seeking forgiveness for personal sins while ensuring justice between people.
